single_change: Placement surface only. S1 placed dots by descending model probability p. S2 places the same number of dots with the same allocator, spacing, allowed mask and budget, but ranks cells by E[k](x) = sum_g p(g) k(d(x,g)) - the convolution of the identical fitted surface with the competition's own 300 m triangular kernel - computed by the shared vendor function gems57.emit.expected_credit on each fold crop and on the final grid. Model, features, fits, seeds, folds, controls, evaluator, budget (37,654), spacing (3 px) and catalogue mask (>2 px) are byte-identical to S1; the cached S1 seed/final surfaces are reused, so no refit and no new canary surface arises.
mechanism: The metric's TP term is a max-cover of truth pixels by kernel-weighted dots, so a dot's expected marginal credit is the probability mass within its 300 m kernel footprint, not the probability of its own cell. Ranking by own-cell p places dots on narrow peaks; ranking by kernel-convolved p places them on local mass centroids, covering truth that is offset from the predicted ridge by rasterization/mapping error (the effect the GEMSDOE32 live-mirror analysis estimated at ~1.85 px scatter). The kernel is the metric's own - S2 introduces no fitted blur, threshold or weight parameter.
named_non_fault_mimic: Unchanged from S1 (facies pinch-out, fan-lobe boundary, survey seam). The emission change can additionally waste dots at the centroid of a broad non-fault probability blob (e.g. a lithologic contact zone) where own-cell ranking would have spread them along its crest.
